s1.syndrome_frame: Multiple skin-colored papules on the face and vulva with a gradual increase in number over time
salient_findings: Multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored asymptomatic papules on the face and vulva
Family history of similar facial papules
Histopathology showing buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 60s
Lesions first appeared around 50 years of age
Approximately 60 lesions are present
Lesions are located on the face and vulva
No palmar or plantar pits were observed
Patient has a history of meningioma
Family history of similar facial papules
Histopathology of lesions shows basaloid cells and small cystic spaces
Clefting between tumor aggregates and surrounding stroma was focally evident
Whole-exome sequencing revealed a conserved splice-site mutation in SUFU gene

shortlist.label: Multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of multiple skin-colored papules on the face and vulva, and the histopathological features of basaloid cells and small cystic spaces, with a family history of similar lesions and a SUFU gene mutation

shortlist.label: Basal cell nevus syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Shares similar clinical features, including multiple basal cell carcinomas, and the patient's history of meningioma is also consistent with this syndrome

shortlist.label: Infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological features of the lesions are consistent with this diagnosis, although the multiple and familial nature of the lesions suggests a hereditary component

shortlist.label: Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to basal cell nevus syndrome, this diagnosis could explain the patient's multiple basal cell carcinomas and family history of similar lesions

shortlist.label: Generalized basaloid follicular hamartoma syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Could be considered due to the presence of multiple basaloid lesions, although the clinical and histopathological features are not as strongly suggestive of this diagnosis as they are for the top 3 options

s4.champion: Multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma syndrome

raw.champion: Multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma syndrome
raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules on the face and vulva, along with a family history of similar lesions and a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene, supports this diagnosis. The histopathology showing buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces also aligns with this condition.

rejected.label: Basal cell nevus syndrome
rejected.why: While basal cell nevus syndrome is a consideration, the absence of palmar or plantar pits and jaw cysts, which are common in this syndrome, makes it less likely.

rejected.label: Infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: This is a type of basal cell carcinoma, but the patient's multiple lesions and family history suggest a more complex syndrome.

rejected.label: Nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome
rejected.why: This is another term for basal cell nevus syndrome, which is less likely due to the absence of characteristic features like palmar or plantar pits.

rejected.label: Generalized basaloid follicular hamartoma syndrome
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by follicular hamartomas, which are not described in the patient's histopathology.
